newsitem.title: USA: Rexene agrees to Huntsman $16/share offer. [corrected 19:30 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Rexene agrees to Huntsman $16/share offer. [corrected 19:30 gmt]

text.p: Rexene Corp and Hunstman Corp said in a joint statement that Rexene had agreed to a $16 per share offer by privately held Huntsman.
The total cost of the deal, including the assumption of debt, is $600 million, the companies said on Monday.
Rexene (corrects from Huntsman) has 19 million shares outstanding and the deal is expected to be completed in the third quarter of this year.
Agreement to the $16 per share offer ends months of wrangling between Rexene and Huntsman and a very public proxy battle fought by Spear Leeds Kellog and Wyser Pratte and Co.

"We have maintained our interest in Rexene because of the extraordinary synergies and efficiencies that would result from a merger of the two companies. We greatly respect (Rexene chief executive) Andy Smith (corrects from "Huntsman CEO" to "Rexene chief executive") and believe Rexene has built strong value in this business," said Hunstman chief executive, Jon Huntsman.
As a result of the definitive agreement between the two company boards, Rexene has cancelled plans for a share buyback tender and cancelled a special shareholder meeting scheduled for this Thursday.
The deal gives Huntsman access to the polyethylene business and Peter Huntsman, the company's chief operating officer, said that future growth would be "controlled, but aggressive."
Huntsman is the largest privately held chemicals company in the U.S. and has $4.3 billion in annual revenues.
